tagline: A small town in a Mae Hong Son valley — sea of fog, rice-field cafes, a walking street, Pai Canyon, and a historic WWII bridge
introHtml:
Pai is a small district in the mountains of Mae Hong Son province that has grown into a laid-back travel town loved by northern Thais and travelers from all over. Its appeal is the cool weather, the terraced rice fields ringed by mountains, the cafes and guesthouses that line the fields, and the evening walking street buzzing with street food and handmade crafts.

Most people in Pai get up early to catch the sea of fog at the Yun Lai viewpoint or Wat Phra That Mae Yen, stop by Pai Canyon at sunset, walk the historic WWII-era bridge, soak at the Tha Pai hot springs, and visit Mo Paeng and Pam Bok waterfalls. Pai suits people who want to slow down — ride a motorbike around on their own, sit in a cafe for hours, and listen to live music at a small bar at night. The road up to Pai is 762 curves from Chiang Mai, so anyone who gets carsick should bring something for it.
bestTime: November–February is cool with thick morning fog — Pai's high season. March–April turns hot and hazy from crop burning. The rainy season, June–October, is lush and green but the winding road gets slippery.

highlights.name: Pai Canyon (Kong Lan)
highlights.blurb: Earthen ravines eroded into narrow ridges you can walk along for mountain views in every direction — Pai's most popular sunset spot.

highlights.name: Pai Historic Bridge
highlights.blurb: A steel bridge across the Pai River built during World War II, now a photo landmark and a check-in point on the way into town.

highlights.name: Yun Lai Viewpoint
highlights.blurb: A morning sea-of-fog spot above Santichon village, where the Pai valley fills with white mist — sip a warm tea and wait for first light.

highlights.name: Tha Pai Hot Springs
highlights.blurb: Natural hot springs in a pine forest, hot enough to cook an egg, with foot-soak pools and a mineral spa to unwind after a full day out.

highlights.name: Santichon Village
highlights.blurb: A Yunnanese Chinese village on a hillside with Chinese earthen houses, a giant swing, tea houses and Yunnan food, and pretty terraced-field views.

highlights.name: Wat Phra That Mae Yen (Big Buddha)
highlights.blurb: A large white Buddha image on a hill — climb the stairs to pay respects and take in a 360-degree view of the whole Pai valley.

foodScene.name: Rice-field and hillside cafes
foodScene.note: Pai is full of fresh-coffee cafes with views of terraced fields and mountains. Many open early for photo-minded visitors, so you can linger over coffee and the view.

foodScene.name: Pai Walking Street
foodScene.note: In the evening the walking street through the center of town fills with street food, grilled bites, sweets, drinks, and handmade crafts from local makers.

foodScene.name: Northern Thai food
foodScene.note: Khao soi, nam ngiao, kaeng hang lay, and nam phrik num are easy to find at local spots in town — proper northern flavors eaten with sticky rice.

foodScene.name: Santichon Yunnan food
foodScene.note: Santichon village serves Yunnanese Chinese dishes like braised pork leg with mantou buns, oolong tea, and mountain Chinese fare that's hard to find elsewhere.

foodScene.name: Vegan and healthy eats
foodScene.note: With its crowd of health-minded travelers, Pai has plenty of vegan spots, smoothie bowls, and clean food — handy for long-stay guests and the wellness crowd.

foodScene.name: Bars and live music
foodScene.note: At night Pai has small bars and live-music spots leaning reggae and folk — an easy-going scene for listening to music and having a drink with new friends.

attractions.name: Pai Canyon (Kong Lan)
attractions.blurb: Narrow earthen ridges you can walk along for mountain views in every direction — a popular sunset spot; mind the thin ridges and crumbly edges.

attractions.name: Pai Historic Bridge
attractions.blurb: A WWII-era steel bridge across the Pai River — a photo landmark and check-in point before you reach the town.

attractions.name: Yun Lai Viewpoint
attractions.blurb: A morning sea-of-fog spot above Santichon where the Pai valley turns into white mist, with a tea house to sit and wait for first light.

attractions.name: Tha Pai Hot Springs
attractions.blurb: Natural hot springs in a pine forest with soaking pools and a mineral spa to relax — a good stop after a full day out.

attractions.name: Santichon Village
attractions.blurb: A Yunnanese Chinese village on a hillside with Chinese earthen houses, a giant swing, tea houses and Yunnan food, and terraced-field views.

attractions.name: Wat Phra That Mae Yen (Big Buddha)
attractions.blurb: A large white Buddha image on a hill — climb the stairs to pay respects and take in a wide view over the whole Pai valley.

attractions.name: Mo Paeng Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A multi-tier waterfall near town with pools to swim in and natural rock slides, shady and easygoing in the forest.

attractions.name: Boon Ko Ku So Bamboo Bridge
attractions.blurb: A long bamboo bridge stretching across rice fields to a hilltop temple — walk over the green paddies for a nature-focused photo spot.
